supporting_observations.claim: The timing is broadly consistent with the approved CaseBinder updater's approximately five-minute update checks, but the available connection records do not identify CaseBinder or any other originating process.
These records show HTTP connections to the internal proxy, not the proxy CONNECT destination or the remote HTTPS service; they therefore do not establish what the alerted connections accessed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records for the alerted connections contain connection timing, byte counts, and the internal proxy address, but no proxy CONNECT target, URL, TLS SNI, or certificate details.
No supplied record attributes the alerted connections to a process or confirms that CaseBinder generated them.
The proxy CONNECT record at 14:17:21 identifies ctldl.windowsupdate.com, but it is outside the alerted 13:30–14:10 interval and does not identify the earlier destinations (T146-00251).
claims_not_established: The destination domain or service for the alerted connections.
Whether the connections were generated by the approved CaseBinder updater or by another application.
Whether the activity transferred malicious content or involved command-and-control, data exfiltration, or other malicious behavior.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy logs for 13:30–14:10 UTC on 2026-09-22, including CONNECT destination, status, and client details.
Endpoint EDR or equivalent process-to-network telemetry for WS-NKIM-01 during the connection times.
CaseBinder updater logs and verification of the installed updater's identity and activity during the interval.
unrelated_findings: At 14:00:34 UTC, WS-NKIM-01 connected to FILE-MAP-01 over SMB and FILE-MAP-01 recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON. Review separately; this does not identify or decide the alerted proxy activity (T146-00164, T146-00168).

A 14:18:33 UserAssist registry value on WS-NKIM-01 appears to encode a reference to C:\Windows\System32\mstsc.exe; review separately if warranted. It is outside the alerted connection pattern (T146-00258).
At 14:19:01 UTC, msiexec.exe accessed services.exe. The supplied event does not establish whether this was expected installation activity; review separately if warranted (T146-00259).
